name: IL-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+12 district lean with strong Democratic fundamentals
Incumbent Schneider has $3M raised and $1.7M cash on hand
Challenger Lambrecht shows no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The D+12 district, incumbent advantage, and a large financial edge for Schneider over an underfunded challenger all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and markets agree at roughly 96%. With no contrary polling or ratings, the fundamentals-based margin of about 22 points stands.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or unexpected outside spending against Schneider would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brad Schneider, the Democratic incumbent in Illinois' 10th District, seeks another term in a suburban Chicago seat that leans Democratic by about 12 points. He has raised over $3 million and holds $1.7 million on hand, while Republican challenger Carl Lambrecht reports no fundraising figures. No outside groups are spending against Schneider, and no independent polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets give Schneider roughly a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals and his incumbency. With no expert ratings or polling to contradict the underlying numbers, the race is rated Safe Democratic, with an expected margin in the low twenties.
